title: Numbers & Counting
description: Class 1 IMO — Numbers & Counting: count, compare and order numbers to 100 with olympiad-style logical reasoning, everyday maths and achievers practice.

topics.title: Counting and Number Names (1 to 100)
topics.concept:
When we count, we say numbers in order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 … all the way to 100. Each number is one more than the number before it.

Numbers also have names. For example, 7 is seven, 14 is fourteen and 40 is forty. Counting forward means going up (2, 3, 4 …) and counting backward means going down (4, 3, 2 …).

examples.solution: Count one more: 29 → 30. The answer is 30.
One less than 12 is 11. So the missing number is 11.

recap: Counting forward adds 1 each time; counting backward subtracts 1.
The number just after a number is 'one more'; just before is 'one less'.

topics.title: Comparing and Ordering Numbers
topics.concept:
To compare two numbers we see which is bigger or smaller. A number with more tens is bigger. If the tens are equal, the one with more ones is bigger.

We can put numbers in order from smallest to largest (ascending) or largest to smallest (descending).
recap: More tens means a bigger number; compare ones only when tens are equal.
Ascending = small → big; descending = big → small.

quiz.explanation: 91 has 9 tens — the most — so it is largest.

quiz.q: Arrange in ascending order: 45, 54, 15. The first (smallest) is ___.
quiz.explanation: 15 has only 1 ten, so it is the smallest.

topics.title: Number Patterns & Reasoning
topics.concept:
Numbers often follow a pattern — a rule that repeats. Skip counting by 2s (2, 4, 6, 8) or by 5s (5, 10, 15, 20) makes patterns. In olympiads you find the rule, then the next number.

You also reason about positions — like who is 2nd or 5th in a line.

examples.solution: The rule is +5 each time, so the next is 25.

examples.problem: In a line, Riya is 3rd from the front. How many children are in front of her?
examples.solution: Being 3rd means 2 children are ahead of her.

recap: Find the rule (e.g. +2, +5, +10), then continue the pattern.
Ordinal numbers (1st, 2nd, 3rd …) tell position, not how many.

quiz.explanation: The rule is +10, so after 30 comes 40.
All are even (skip-counting by 2) except 7, which is odd.

questions.explanation: 23 has 2 tens and 3 ones — the smallest here.

questions.q: How many tens are in the number 70?
Find the next number in the pattern: 3, 6, 9, 12, ___ ?
questions.explanation: The rule is +3, so after 12 comes 15.

questions.q: Which one is the odd one out?  10, 20, 25, 30
If 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C, then 2, 1, 3 spells ___ ?
A line has 6 children. Aarav is 4th from the front. How many are behind him?
questions.explanation: 4 are up to Aarav, so 6 − 4 = 2 are behind.
